title: Cost Ops: Auto-rollout Sprint Hub for Adaptive Batching, KV Temporalization, and Quant Profiles
creator: Priya Desai
summary: Create a lightweight initiative tracker and automated rollout pipeline to coordinate experiments and canary deployments for batching, KV temporalization (time-based KV lifecycle), and quantization profiles across Dedicated and Hosted environments.
description: Motivation: ad-hoc experiments across teams produce fractured learnings and slow adoption. We need a single hub to coordinate cost-reduction experiments (adaptive batching heuristics, KV temporalization TTLs and eviction strategies, and quantization candidate rollouts), automate canary rollouts, and capture acceptance criteria and telemetry so PM/Eng/Design can move faster and safely. Scope: tracker UI + templated experiment spec, standardized telemetry contract, an automated canary pipeline (staged rollout, automated guardrail checks), and a lightweight field notebook capturing model- and route-level results.
success_metrics: >60% adoption of recommended quant profiles in pilot teams within 8 weeks
Number of failed rollouts <= 1 per quarter
acceptance_criteria: Tracker template created and validated by two ENG squads and Design
Canary pipeline runs end-to-end with canary -> ramp -> steady states and automatic rollback on threshold breaches
Telemetry schema published (tokens, cost, latency, correctness checks) and integrated into Console dashboards
Two field experiments completed (one batching heuristic + one quant profile) with documented learnings and next steps
updates: 2025-02-10 — Kickoff meeting: aligned on goals with SRE, Runtime, and Console teams. Action: ENG-1842 to prototype telemetry contract.
2025-02-18 — Prototype tracker spec submitted; Design has mockups (DES-122). PM asked to prioritize TTL + eviction heuristics for KV temporalization as first experiment.

2025-02-25 — Runtime team completed initial adaptive batching prototype (ENG-4120). Early lab runs show 12% median token cost reduction for chat-small routes; no p95 latency regression in synthetic tests.
2025-03-03 — Integration spike: connected telemetry to Console dev dashboard. Found mismatch in token attribution for multi-plugin requests; created ENG-4289 to investigate attribution bug.

2025-03-05 — Decision to run two simultaneous pilots: (A) adaptive batching on low-latency routes with aggressive micro-batching; (B) conservative quant profile for embed-small on Dedicated. Canary plan drafted.
2025-03-05 — Blocker: design sign-off pending on tracker UX for experiment metadata; follow-up scheduled with Design on 2025-03-07.
risks: Regressions in output quality after quantization not caught by low-coverage automated checks
Unexpected p95 latency spikes for certain tail-length prompts when batching thresholds change
Coordination overhead between Hosted and Dedicated runtime variants could slow rollouts
Telemetry gaps causing mis-attribution of savings to wrong routes or models
decisions: Adopt staged canary with three buckets: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% traffic, rollback if cost reduction < 3% or p95 latency > 5% above baseline
Require at least one subjective eval task + automated unit tests for quality before any quant profile moves beyond canary
Prioritize KV temporalization TTL experiments for chat-style workloads where prefix reuse is common
Keep rollout orchestration minimal (serverless job + webhook) for initial phase, iterate to more integrated pipeline after two successful rollouts
next_steps: ENG-4120: finalize batching config schema and publish experiment template (target: 2025-03-12)
DES-122: deliver final tracker mockups and a short interaction spec (target: 2025-03-07)
ENG-1842: complete telemetry contract and wire basic Console widgets (target: 2025-03-14)
Schedule pilot kickoff with pilot teams (Growth + Search) and agree on evaluation prompts and key slices (target: 2025-03-11)
Create rollback playbook doc and alerting runbook (owner: On-call SRE)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Dry-run in dev with synthetic traffic and end-to-end telemetry validation
Stage 1 (Canary): 0.5% traffic for 24h with automated guardrail checks (cost delta, p95 latency, unit-quality tests)
Stage 2 (Ramp): 5% traffic for 48h if canary passes; add subjective eval batch
Stage 3: 25% traffic for 72h; if stable, promote to steady-state and schedule postmortem
Automatic rollback triggers: cost regression, p95 latency > 5% above baseline, >0.5% increase in failed completions or hallucination checks
notes: We should avoid one-size-fits-all quant profiles; plan to surface route-by-route recommended profiles in Console.
Consider a lightweight experiment 'scorecard' view that shows per-route cost delta, latency delta, and quality delta in a single row for quick triage.
Longer-term: integrate this hub with the Optimize recommendations engine so experiments can be suggested automatically based on usage patterns.
Follow-up: sync with Legal if any telemetry contains customer PII; currently telemetry contract excludes request payloads, only metadata and aggregate metrics are used.
